author: mardsouza
body:
#### PR description:

`GenXSecAnalyzer` currently derives its cross section from `LHERunInfoProduct`, which for certain Powheg samples is the *inclusive* value and does not include the branching ratio applied later by Pythia. This makes the reported cross section inconsistent with references for affected samples.

An investigation compared `LHERunInfoProduct`, `GenRunInfoProduct`, and `LHEEventProduct` across several generators (Powheg+Pythia, Pythia-only, MadGraph MadSpin/MLM/FXFX+Pythia, Sherpa). Summary of findings:
- `LHEEventProduct` is not universally available (missing for Sherpa/Pythia-only) and not a reliable generator-independent estimator, so it is kept only as a diagnostic, not used for the reported value. It is only reliable for Powheg+Pythia, and even there it's *uncertainty* is an artifact of alternating-sign event weights, not a real statistical error. For other generators (e.g. MadGraph) it can store unrelated information, off by up to ~1e5.
- `GenRunInfoProduct` cross section *value* is always correct (includes the BR), but its uncertainty, traced to Pythia8's `ProcessContainer::sigmaDelta()`, mixes a veto-efficiency term already accounted for elsewhere in `GenXSecAnalyzer` and a weight-variance term (found to be zero in all tested samples).

Based on this, the fix implemented is:
- Cross section **value** is taken from `GenRunInfoProduct` when available.
- Cross section **uncertainty** is taken from `LHERunInfoProduct` and scaled by `(GenRunInfoProduct) / (LHERunInfoProduct)`, avoiding double-counting of the veto-efficiency uncertainty already propagated downstream.
- If `GenRunInfoProduct` is absent, behavior falls back unchanged to the previous `LHERunInfoProduct`-only calculation.
- A new untracked `verbose` `bool` parameter (default `false`) prints a detailed breakdown of `LHERunInfoProduct`, `GenRunInfoProduct`, and `LHEEventProduct` (mean/RMS of `originalXWGTUP()`, read via a newly implemented `analyze()`) for debugging/validation.
- Final log lines are tagged `[LHE]`/`[GEN]` to indicate the source of the reported cross section.

**Output change:** the `"final cross section = "` line format is unchanged (verified against the [XSDB import script](https://github.com/cms-sw/xsecdb/blob/master/scripts/xsec_calc_auto/3_convert_outputs.py)), only its value is corrected for affected samples  no downstream XSDB changes needed.

**Dependencies:** none beyond existing `GenRunInfoProduct`/`LHEEventProduct` data formats already produced by standard generator/LHE workflows.

**Additional material**:
    - [Indico presentation with full per-sample validation log](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1681846/#9-genxsecanalyzer-cross-sectio)
    - [GitLab repo to track the development of the related task](https://gitlab.cern.ch/desousma/gen-tasklist-issue70)
    - [CMS-GEN GitLab Task that originated this PR](https://gitlab.cern.ch/cms-gen/gen_tasklist/-/work_items/70)
    - [Documentation on how to use this new version of GenXSecAnalyzer](https://cms-generators.docs.cern.ch/useful-tools-and-links/HowToGenXSecAnalyzer/)

#### PR validation:

Ran over samples from Powheg+Pythia, MadGraph (MadSpin/MLM/FXFX)+Pythia, Pythia-only, and Sherpa:
- Powheg+Pythia samples affected by the BR issue now match reference cross sections.
- Unaffected samples reproduce the previous cross section (within a few % for some MadGraph samples), confirming no regression.
- `LHEEventProduct` mean/RMS (verbose mode) cross-checked against `GenRunInfoProduct` as an independent diagnostic.
- XSDB `.json` ingestion verified identical in structure before/after, with only the corrected value changing.
title: GeneratorInterface/Core: Fix cross section consistency in GenXSecAnalyzer
